SALONpainting, illustration & the light between

About this collection

A personal image board — paintings and illustrations kept for their light, atmosphere, presence, handling and colour. Open it and wander: every visit shuffles the works; click one to see more by the same hand.

It began as a directory of contemporary painterly figuration, held between two poles: the sealed quiet of 森本草介 — a still figure, soft even light — and the performed anguish of 鴨居玲, a figure lit against darkness, despair staged rather than diagnosed. A recurring thread runs between them: the figure seen through something — water, steam, glass, haze (三重野慶, Alyssa Monks, Casey Baugh).

The illustration side carries the same appetite for light: translucent, backlit gradients (白身魚, loundraw, カントク, DSマイル) and, at the other end, designed colour and graphic energy (米山舞, 望月けい, Mika Pikazo, LAM, redjuice).

Those are starting points, not fences. Newer additions reach sideways — atmospheric interiors and landscapes, prints, drawings, stylised figuration — wherever one strong quality connects. Painters also includes a few historical sources of those qualities (Zorn, Whistler, Sargent, Hammershøi, 吉田博), all from museum open-access collections. Each artist page keeps its sources.
